claims.text: Rapid quenching can promote formation of an amorphous-like structure in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
A sub-Tg relaxation anneal immediately after rapid quenching will improve amorphous retention and thermal stability in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The proposed anneal should be conducted approximately 50 K below Tg for 10–15 minutes in an inert environment.
The sub-Tg anneal will relieve internal stresses in the as-quenched amorphous structure.
The sub-Tg anneal will reduce excess free volume in the as-quenched amorphous structure.
Relaxing internal strain and lowering the glass enthalpy below Tg will reduce the driving force for devitrification.
Reducing the driving force for devitrification will increase the crystallization-onset temperature during reheating.
Amorphous material is metastable and can crystallize during heating when activation barriers are overcome.
Annealed specimens will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature than unannealed Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 specimens.
Annealed specimens will have a lower crystallization enthalpy than unannealed specimens.
Annealed specimens will retain more amorphous phase during thermal analysis than unannealed specimens.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits complex crystallization and thermal behavior.
Unannealed Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 has limited amorphous retention and rapidly devitrifies under modest reheating.
The anneal will be effective after cooling at rates from tens to thousands of kelvin per second and during reheating up to near Tg.
Very slow cooling or reheating significantly above Tg will diminish the effectiveness of the anneal.
The optimum relaxation temperature and dwell time depend on purity, specimen geometry, and thermal history.
